caption_fb:
When you look at your own website every day, it is easy to miss the simple things that confuse first-time visitors. A crowded navigation bar or leading with your company history instead of the customer's problem can quietly cut your leads in half.

If you want a fresh set of eyes on your site, I am recording a few quick video reviews this week. No sales pitch—just practical fixes you can make in an afternoon.

caption_li:
Most website friction is completely invisible to the business owner.

When a site is built around what you want to say rather than what a prospective client needs to find, conversion rates drop. Minor design choices—like a crowded mobile menu or an unclear hero headline—force buyers to look at competitors.

If you want to identify where your site is losing potential clients, I can help.

Send me a direct message with the word AUDIT. I will record a 3-minute video highlighting two practical structural changes you can make this week.

When was the last time you tested your website on a mobile device as a first-time visitor?

slides.title: 3 small website mistakes killing your sales right now.
slides.body: Most owners check their site on a laptop, ignoring how real buyers navigate. If your pages have these specific flaws, visitors leave without booking or buying.

slides.title: Your homepage leads with your company history.
slides.body: Buyers do not care that you opened in 2012. If your main headline says 'Welcome to Our Firm' instead of what you fix, visitors bounce in 3 seconds.

slides.title: Your mobile menu has more than five items.
slides.body: On a phone, a long menu takes up the full screen. When buyers get overwhelmed by options, they close the tab instead of tapping your contact button.
